chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who accused a group of men of adultery. He said: If they bring him together [in one session], he is given one hadd punishment. And if they bring him separately [in different sessions], a hadd punishment is given to each one individually.
ai.seo_question: How many punishments does an accuser receive for falsely accusing a group of men?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies the application of hadd al-qadhf (flogging) when a single accuser targets a group, distinguishing between a collective accusation in one setting versus separate accusations in different gatherings. It reflects the juristic principle that the punishment is tied to the distinct acts of accusation rather than the number of defendants, ensuring legal precision in Shia fiqh. The ruling underscores the importance of procedural context in determining the severity of the penalty for false testimony.
